properties.natural_language: All incoming P2P block data requests via eth/70 must have their requested block numbers validated to be >= 15,537,393 (Paris upgrade boundary) before processing.
GetBlockBodies (0x05) and GetReceipts (0x0f) messages must be rejected if they target blocks below the Paris upgrade boundary (block 15,537,393).
Rate limiting must be enforced on incoming P2P block data request volume to prevent resource exhaustion from peers requesting excessive data.
After a pre-PoS data request is identified (block < 15,537,393), the request must be rejected and no block data must be served.
After a post-PoS data request is validated (block >= 15,537,393), the requested block bodies or receipts must be retrieved and returned to the peer.
After protocol upgrade to eth/70, the client must refuse to serve any pre-PoS block data regardless of the message type (GetBlockBodies, BlockBodies, GetReceipts, Receipts).
The Paris upgrade boundary block number (15,537,393) must be immutable and consistently applied across all block data request validation paths.
During the mixed protocol network state, eth/70 clients must not be affected by coexisting eth/69 clients and must independently enforce post-PoS-only data serving.
The rejection mechanism for pre-PoS data requests must be defined: either silent drop or explicit error message, applied consistently.
Clients must be able to reliably distinguish PoS from pre-PoS block numbers using the Paris upgrade boundary.
Out-of-band data retrieval mechanisms (archive nodes, Era files) must be available for pre-PoS historical data access.
Standard P2P security considerations must apply including DoS protection against mixed-protocol network attacks.
The bootstrap checkpoint root must be obtained from a trusted source (weak subjectivity assumption) before light client initialization.
The LightClientBootstrap object returned from a full node must be cryptographically verified against the checkpoint root before initializing the light client store.
All LightClientUpdate objects must be validated against sync committee signatures with at least 2/3 supermajority before advancing the finalized header.
Responses from P2P peers serving light client data must be cryptographically verified, and multiple peers should be queried to prevent eclipse attacks.
After successful bootstrap, the light client store must contain a valid trusted header and current sync committee, enabling update processing.
After processing a valid LightClientUpdate, the finalized header must advance to the update's finalized header if it represents a newer finalization.
After detecting a fork epoch boundary, the light client store data structures must be upgraded to the new fork format before processing any new-fork updates.
The light client must always maintain at least one trusted header and sync committee once bootstrapped, and must never regress to an earlier finalized slot.
Fork version transitions in light client data structures must be correctly handled: each fork's dedicated spec defines exact field additions and transformations.
Full nodes serving light client data (via req/resp and gossip) must prepare data correctly according to the sync protocol specs.
The eth_requestAccounts RPC call must trigger an explicit user consent dialog before exposing any account addresses to the requesting DApp.
The user consent dialog must be browser-isolated from DApp JavaScript manipulation and must display the accurate requesting origin.
The caller context (origin, permissions state) must be validated before checking existing permissions for the requesting DApp.
After user approval, the resolved promise must contain an Array of at least one valid Ethereum account address string.
After user rejection, the promise must be rejected with an informative Error object.
Permission caching must be per-origin: a permission granted to one DApp origin must not be accessible to a different origin.
No account addresses may be exposed to any DApp without prior explicit user consent, regardless of provider availability.
The provider implementation must faithfully display the requesting origin to the user in the consent dialog, preventing origin spoofing.
Repeated eth_requestAccounts calls after user rejection must not bypass consent requirements; implementations should respect user fatigue.
EIP-150 gas repricing must be applied for all IO-heavy operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) at post-Tangerine Whistle blocks (>= 2,463,000).
Block number must be checked against 2,463,000 threshold during block processing to determine which gas cost schedule applies.
After applying EIP-150 rules, IO-heavy operations must cost more gas than pre-fork, making DoS attacks economically infeasible.
After gas deduction using the new cost schedule, transactions with insufficient gas for repriced operations must result in an out-of-gas exception.
Gas costs must accurately reflect the computational cost of IO operations to prevent resource exhaustion attacks.
All network participants must apply the same gas cost schedule for a given block number to maintain consensus.
No alternative underpriced operations should exist that could achieve similar DoS effects after repricing.
Block difficulty validation must verify the claimed difficulty matches the expected difficulty computed using EIP-649 rules (fake block number with 3M offset for post-Byzantium).
For post-Byzantium blocks, the fake block number must be computed as max(0, block_number - 3,000,000) before calculating the ice age component.
After difficulty validation, blocks with difficulty mismatch (claimed != expected) must be rejected.
After block reward computation for post-Byzantium blocks, the miner base reward must be exactly 3 ETH (3e18 wei), and uncle rewards must use the formula (8-k) * 3 ETH / 8.
All clients must implement the difficulty calculation and reward changes identically to maintain consensus.
The reduced block reward (3 ETH) must maintain sufficient mining incentive for network security.
window.isSecureContext must be true before the Ethereum provider is injected into any web page.
The page origin must be potentially trustworthy per W3C Secure Contexts spec (HTTPS, localhost, file://) before provider injection.

Third-party iframes must be blocked from provider access by default. Only first-party same-origin iframes without restrictive sandbox or explicitly permissioned third-party iframes should gain access.
After an insecure context is detected (isSecureContext === false), the provider must be blocked and window.ethereum must remain undefined.
After all security checks pass (secure context + trustworthy origin), the provider must be injected and window.ethereum must be defined.
After a first-party iframe passes sandbox compatibility check (no sandbox or allow-same-origin present), the provider must be allowed.
Developer mode must default to disabled. HTTP localhost access to the provider requires explicit developer mode enablement.
The browser must correctly implement and report window.isSecureContext for the provider security checks to be effective.
BLS-to-execution-change gossip messages must be validated against current_epoch >= CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH before any further processing.
Each node must track the first valid signed BLS-to-execution-change per validator index and reject duplicates.
All BLS-to-execution-change messages must pass full process_bls_to_execution_change validation before acceptance and forwarding.
Capella beacon block gossip messages must have their fork digest verified to match the expected Capella fork digest.
Fork version for block request/response serialization must be correctly determined via compute_fork_version based on the block's epoch.
After all validation passes, the BLS-to-execution-change message must be accepted for future block inclusion and forwarded to gossip peers.
After determining the fork version, the block response must be serialized in the correct fork-specific format (Phase0, Altair, Bellatrix, or Capella).
An attacker must not be able to forge valid BLS signatures for bls_to_execution_change messages to redirect withdrawal credentials.
Wall-clock time used for epoch calculation must be reasonably synchronized across nodes for consistent gossip propagation.
The size parameter for byte padding operations must be a valid non-negative integer to prevent unexpected behavior.
Size parameters passed to byte padding operations must be bounded to reasonable values to prevent memory exhaustion.
After left-pad or right-pad operation, the result must be exactly the target size, padded with zero bytes on the appropriate side.
When the input value length is greater than or equal to the target size, the original value must be returned unmodified (no truncation).
The validator client must be completely stopped and not signing any messages before importing a slashing protection interchange file.
The interchange file must pass JSON schema validation before any data extraction or import processing.
The genesis_validators_root in the interchange file must match the current network's genesis_validators_root before records are merged.
All BLS public keys in the interchange file must be validated as valid BLS12-381 public keys.
Block signing requests must be checked against the slashing protection database: block slot must be >= minimum previously signed slot, and no conflicting block signature may exist.
Attestation signing requests must be checked for surround voting: source epoch >= minimum and target epoch >= minimum, with no surrounding attestation detected.
After a genesis root mismatch is detected, the import must be rejected entirely with no records merged.
After successful record merge, the slashing protection database must contain the union of previous and imported records, with minimums updated.
After signing a block, the slot and signing root must be recorded in the slashing protection database before the signed block is released.
After signing an attestation, the source/target epochs and signing root must be recorded in the slashing protection database.
Missing signing roots in interchange data must be treated as potential conflicts (conservative interpretation), blocking signing at those slots/epochs.
Duplicate public keys in the interchange file data array must be safely merged, combining all their signed_blocks and signed_attestations records.
An attacker must not be able to trigger interchange file import while the validator is actively signing.
All provider.request() calls from DApps must have their RequestArguments validated (method field required) before routing to the Wallet.
All data from untrusted DApps entering the Provider must be sanitized and rate-limited before processing.
After a connect event, the chainId must be emitted in hex format to all listening DApps.
After a disconnect event, a ProviderRpcError with appropriate code (4900 or 4901) must be emitted to all listening DApps.
After user revokes account access, the accountsChanged event must be emitted with an empty accounts array, and eth_accounts must return empty.
The Provider must not contain any private user data. Provider and Wallet programs must remain isolated from each other.
All ProviderRpcError objects must conform to the standardized error code format (4001, 4100, 4200, 4900, 4901) with appropriate code, message, and optional data fields.
The Provider object exposed at window.ethereum must not be modifiable by DApp JavaScript after injection.
